key_insight: VideoAtlas represents long videos as a hierarchical, lossless grid that lets models navigate content with logarithmic compute cost, giving an immediate visual overview without captions or heavy preprocessing.
problem_solved: Existing video-language extensions either compress visual information into lossy summaries or collapse long context into text, losing fidelity and scaling poorly for long-form video.
method: Encode video into a multi-scale hierarchical grid that preserves full visual information while supporting coarse-to-fine access patterns.
Provide a task-agnostic, navigable environment (no captioning or custom preprocessing) so downstream models can fetch only the needed regions.
Use multiscale indexing and navigation algorithms to achieve logarithmic compute/time complexity when querying long timelines.
impact: Enables scalable, high-fidelity long-video understanding and interaction for models and applications, reducing compute and preprocessing overhead while preserving visual detail for downstream tasks.
visual_elements: Hierarchical grid diagram showing full-frame → tiles → zoomed tiles to illustrate lossless multiscale representation
Zoomable timeline mockup demonstrating coarse-to-fine navigation and quick overview at a glance
Compute scaling chart comparing logarithmic (VideoAtlas) vs. linear compute cost as video length increases
Before/after fidelity example: conventional captioned-summary vs. VideoAtlas tile retrieval showing preserved visual detail
paper_title: VideoAtlas: Navigating Long-Form Video in Logarithmic Compute
paper_authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Ali Habibullah, Yazan Alshoibi, Lama Ayash, Tanveer Hussain
